clue.text: Such a net works loose

indicators.note: works as in being worked over or kneaded, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishing or hair net that has worked itself loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like it describes the net, but it is the definition in its old moral sense; 'works' signals the anagram of SUCH A NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose in the old-fashioned moral sense describes someone sexually promiscuous, the opposite of chaste.

clue.text: Administer a beating at Westminster?

parts.note: reads as flogging someone in Parliament, but points to the party officer at Westminster who keeps members in line, named after the tool for beating

explanation.surface: Someone is thrashed in the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the seat of the UK Parliament, where each party's whip enforces voting discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip is both an instrument for flogging and the parliamentary officer who enforces party discipline.

clue.text: Loan shark employer admits game is up

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: one who employs something is its user

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: A moneylender's boss lets slip that the game is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is rugby union; 'is up' reverses it because this is a down clue, and 'admits' means the employer holds it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate interest, just as a loan shark does.

clue.text: He may resort to bars and clubs, but should be fit

definitions.text: He may resort to bars and clubs, but should be fit

parts.words: He may resort to bars and clubs, but should be fit
parts.note: suggests a drinker frequenting pubs and nightclubs, but the bars are parallel or horizontal apparatus bars and the clubs are Indian clubs swung in athletic exercise

explanation.surface: A man who frequents pubs and nightclubs ought nonetheless to keep in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete performing on apparatus such as bars and with clubs must be physically fit.

clue.text: He usually has a second helping

definitions.text: He usually has a second helping

parts.words: He usually has a second helping
parts.note: sounds like a greedy diner, but the second is the assistant who attends a fighter in an affair of honour

explanation.surface: A greedy diner typically goes back for more food.
explanation.definitionFit: In formal combat with pistols or swords, each fighter is attended by a second who helps arrange it.

clue.text: Equip old fellow for the final battle

parts.note: to equip with weapons is to arm
old means aged
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: Kit out an elderly man for the last fight.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Revelation, this is the site of the last decisive battle between good and evil.

clue.text: Fed up, having to stop on guard

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before reversal
to stop is to end

explanation.surface: A guard who is fed up and wants to quit his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF; 'having to' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend something is to guard it against attack.

clue.text: Honestly in distress, trying to avoid publicity

indicators.note: in distress suggests something damaged or troubled, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone sincerely upset is trying to keep out of the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something secretly, so nobody notices, is avoiding publicity.

clue.text: Allow more line to run out to the fish

definitions.text: Allow more line to run out to the fish

parts.words: Allow more line to run out to the fish
parts.note: an angler paying out line from the reel to a hooked fish

explanation.surface: An angler pays out line to a fighting fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To let line run off a fishing reel is to undo the winding on it.

clue.text: Port is left in it, in more than one way

definitions.text: Port is left in it, in more than one way

parts.words: Port is left in it, in more than one way
parts.note: port is the left side of a vessel, and port wine or a port of call can also be left aboard or behind by a vessel

explanation.surface: A decanter of port left inside something, in several senses.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the nautical word for the left-hand side of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a term for the left side of a seagoing vessel, which also carries cargo such as port wine.

clue.text: Phone the boss — he's responsible

parts.note: to phone someone is to ring them
the boss is the leader

explanation.surface: Call your manager, since he is the one to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: The instigator of a plot or riot is the one held responsible for it.

clue.text: It shows pressure or bias is developing

indicators.note: something developing is changing its form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Something reveals that pressure or prejudice is building up.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, lines joining points of equal atmospheric pressure show its distribution.

clue.text: Boycotts a hypocrite, the family ne'er-do-well

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as in a trade-union action
Uriah Heep is the archetypal hypocrite in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A family's disgrace shuns a two-faced relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep, the 'ever so humble' clerk in David Copperfield, is a byword for hypocrisy.
explanation.definitionFit: The member of a family regarded as a disgrace is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Posts include gratuity and wages

indicators.note: include means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a gratuity is a tip

explanation.surface: Jobs come with tips on top of pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posts' looks like jobs, but it is the verb: sends.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary, especially a clergyman's, so these are wages.

clue.text: Why answer?

parts.note: asks for the word that typically answers the question why

explanation.surface: Why should I reply?
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction giving a reason is the standard reply to a question asking why.

clue.text: Demonstrate to member what females had to do to lie in

definitions.text: what females had to do to lie in

parts.note: to demonstrate is to show
a member of the body, such as a leg; here taken as a leg

explanation.surface: Showing a body part, women once had to prove themselves to stay in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Naval lore: women allowed aboard could stay in their hammocks if they put out a leg, proving they were not sailors shirking.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval call to show a leg let women aboard ship stay in their hammocks by proving their sex.

clue.text: The boss went without head pupil

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud

indicators.note: without its head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: The head teacher left, leaving the head pupil in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not a manager but a decorative knob, a stud; 'without head' drops the W of WENT, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is a pupil, someone being taught.

clue.text: Even so, I'd resolved to take the plunge

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken down and reformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Despite everything, I had made up my mind to go for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' reads as determined, but signals an anagram of EVEN SO I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dive steeply downward, nose first, is literally to take the plunge.

clue.text: Secret police observe postage irregularities

indicators.note: irregularities suggests letters out of their proper order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Undercover agents note anomalies in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: Personal column

parts.note: looks like the newspaper's personal ads, but means the column of vertebrae each person has

explanation.surface: The personal ads in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine is a column of bones belonging to each person.

clue.text: A flimsy perch

parts.note: something flimsy is light

explanation.surface: A thin and insubstantial roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to settle or land.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to settle or land on something, as a bird perches.

clue.text: Angle brackets in the end

indicators.note: brackets is a verb here: one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: Angled brackets at the close of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angle brackets' reads as the punctuation marks; split it, with 'Angle' as a verb and 'brackets' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The finish of something is its end.

clue.text: Fire escape on board ship

parts.note: suggests an emergency exit from a burning vessel, but means the outlet for smoke from a ship's boilers

explanation.surface: An emergency exit from a blaze on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's smokestack lets smoke and gases from its furnaces escape.

clue.text: Upset there is — and dismay

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: An upset is there, and dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to dismay them, causing them to lose heart.

clue.text: Having nothing on a dark horse, back the favourite finally

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a dun is a horse of dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter

explanation.surface: Betting nothing on an outsider and backing the favourite at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like betting talk but turns DUN into NUD; 'finally' gives the E of favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing no clothes is naked.

clue.text: A man for one season

parts.note: a man's name that is also, for example, a name for the Christmas season

explanation.surface: A man who appears for only one season.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël is French for Christmas, and the word is also a man's first name.

clue.text: Breathe with difficulty and gag

definitions.meaning: to breathe noisily and with difficulty, as an asthmatic does
a gag is a joke or clever scheme

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rasping breath and, in British slang, a clever trick or joke.

clue.text: Jam book behind piano

indicators.note: behind means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to book a seat is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Jam for a book placed behind the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserve is a fruit jam or conserve.
